title: Open Rank Position in Labor and Public Economics
description:
The Department of Economics at Rice University in Houston, Texas,
invites applications for a tenured or tenure-track faculty position
in Labor Economics and/or Public Economics, beginning July 1, 2027.
The rank is open. Candidates at the Assistant Professor level
should have completed the Ph.D. in Economics or a closely related
field by the date of appointment. Candidates at the Associate or
Full Professor level should have a record of scholarship
commensurate with appointment at that rank at a leading research
department.

We seek a scholar whose research addresses substantive questions in
labor or public economics, broadly defined, including but not
limited to human capital formation over the life cycle,
intergenerational mobility, the design and evaluation of tax and
transfer programs, labor market institutions and wage-setting, and
the labor market
consequences of technological change. Both empirical and structural
approaches are welcome. The successful candidate will join a
department with substantial depth in applied microeconomics and
will have opportunities for collaboration through the Center for
Economic Mobility.

Responsibilities include research, teaching at the undergraduate
and graduate levels, and service to the Department and the
University. Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum
vitae, job market paper or representative publications, and a
teaching statement. Applications received by November 15, 2026,
will receive full consideration.

Also, in our candidate pools, we seek to attract greater
representation of women, scholars of color, people with
disabilities, veterans, and others who have historically been
underrepresented in Economics. Rice is located in Houston, one of
the most diverse metropolitan areas in the United States.

Rice University is an Equal Opportunity Employer with
commitment to diversity at all levels, and considers for employment
qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age,
sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic
origin, genetic information, disability or protected veteran
status.
